gaps.title: Props are not planted
gaps.detail: Every piece of set dressing sits at a nominal height with no grounding pass, so the field reads as assets laid on a flat cloth. Sample terrain height and normal for every prop, sink it slightly, give each a contact shadow. Rubric: nothing floats.

events.note: Contact pools rebuilt in src/art/props.js. Cause found by measurement, not guesswork: the old pool was exactly the prop's own footprint, so from the gameplay camera it was ~95 percent hidden UNDER the prop (proved by tinting the pool mesh red, shots/P04-before). Now: every pool is 1.8x the footprint for tall props and 1.2-1.3x for low ones (rocks, bushes, hedges, earth beds), leans away from the sun (kit.setSun, meadow passes rig.dir), is lifted clear of the ground mesh by the worst tangent-plane deviation actually sampled round it, and MULTIPLIES the ground (dst*(1-a*(1-tint))) instead of alpha-blending flat dark green, so grass keeps its hue and the pool can never wash out. A coarse world grid caps how much shade may stack so a hedgerow of 80 overlapping pools cannot become a black band (peak 1.28 demo / 1.41 meadow against a cap of 1.15). Buildings had NO pool at all: meadow.js now gives the cottage and the three village houses one. Measured with a pixel diff of the same frame with pools on vs off: demo prop-yard 17.0 percent of the frame changes, mean luminance ratio 0.787 on changed pixels (21 percent darker), max darkening 144 of 255; /index.html cottage yard 22.2 percent of the frame changes, max darkening 210 of 255. Counts: 404 pools in the demo, 498 in the meadow, 260 in Puddlewick. Shots: shots/P04-r3/03-prop-yard.png vs 04-prop-yard-NO-pools.png (same camera, __DQ.contacts(false)); shots/P04-index-r4/07-cottage-yard.png. Both harness runs exit 0, 0 console/page errors, 120 fps demo / 116 fps game, 79 draw calls demo.

FINAL evidence set: shots/P04-final/03-prop-yard.png vs shots/P04-final/04-prop-yard-NO-pools.png (identical camera, the only difference is __DQ.contacts(false)); shots/P04-index-final/01-opening.png and 07-cottage-yard.png. Pixel diff of that pair: 17.0 percent of the frame changes, mean luminance ratio 0.787 on changed pixels, max darkening 144 of 255. Cost measured in the running meadow: the whole grounding pass is ONE extra draw call and 996 triangles (119 vs 118 calls, 212742 vs 211746 tris). Harness: demo exit 0 (120 fps, 79 calls), /index.html exit 0 (115.5 fps), 0 console errors, 0 page errors, 0 failed requests.

MEASURED IN /index.html AND demos/P04.html, not eyeballed. (a) Scene hooked through three r180 and traversed: mesh contactShadows exists, visible, 498 instances in the meadow / 404 in the demo, renderOrder 2, CustomBlending DstColor x OneMinusSrcAlpha, depthWrite off. (b) Per-instance grounding sweep: world AABB base of 305 sampled prop instances raycast against the ground mesh -> MEDIAN GAP -0.057 (props sit 5.7cm INTO the ground, not above it); no tuft, flower, fence, barrel, crate, well, bench, rock, picket or building instance exceeded +6cm. The 50 rows above +6cm are all legitimately airborne sub-meshes (lanternGlow halos 10, character face 9, sheep/laneSheep heads 7, canopy outline hulls 6) or merged draw buckets whose centroid is meaningless. (c) A/B with the pool mesh hidden and shown at identical cameras, directional pixel measurement: trees view, hiding the pools BRIGHTENS 16.61 percent of the frame by a mean of 25.4/255 (max 169) and darkens only 1.85 percent; the noise-floor control (same camera, pools left on, same wait) is 2.05 percent brightened vs 2.18 percent darkened, i.e. symmetric wind noise. Signal is 8x the control and one-directional. Cottage yard at pitch 10: 4.65 percent brightened vs 2.13 percent darkened against a 2.55/2.57 control - weaker because that frame is mostly empty lawn, but still asymmetric. (d) Visually confirmed in shots/P04-critic-c1/game/32-28-rep-NW.png: a soft dark pool under every trunk and under each bush of the hedgerow. Shots: 05/06/07 (trees ON, OFF, ON-again control), 02/03/04 (yard). Nothing in the field floats. This gap is closed.

ROUND-2 REGRESSION CHECK, still fixed. Re-measured in /index.html. (a) Grounding sweep over 259 sampled prop instances: world AABB base raycast against the ground mesh gives MEDIAN GAP -0.060 (props sit 6cm INTO the ground). The 30 rows above +6cm are all legitimately airborne or meaningless: character face meshes (9 rows, 0.68-1.19), npc:pan, signs (sign boards on posts, 1.18), and merged draw buckets bucket-tile / bucket-brick whose centroid spans the whole map. No tuft, flower, fence, rock, barrel, crate, bench, mushroom, molehill, stook, wall or gate instance floats. (b) contactShadows mesh alive: 715 instances in the meadow (up from 498 - the new scatter got pools too), visible true, renderOrder 2, CustomBlending, depthWrite false; 455 in demos/P04.html. (c) Visually confirmed at shots/P04-critic-c2/game-b/14-14-rep-NW.png and 16-16-rep-SE.png: a soft dark pool under every trunk, every bush of the hedgerow, every molehill and every mushroom cluster. Nothing floats.

gaps.title: See-through is a dotted checkerboard
gaps.detail: Trees and cottages near the lens dissolve as a screen-door dither across 20-50 percent of the frame, and it triggers on objects not covering the hero. Rebuild kit.updateSee in src/art/props.js plus Toon.see in src/art/toon.js as a clean alpha fade at 35-45 percent with the ink outline kept, eased over 150ms, only for meshes actually covering the hero on screen.

events.note: kit.updateSee rebuilt in src/art/props.js as a CLEAN ALPHA GHOST, and the Bayer dither is switched off rather than handed back. Three new meshes per grove tier, created only when something actually fades: gdepth (depth pre-pass, colour off, pushed back a hair, and it is the mesh that keeps casting the tree's sun shadow), ghull (the shared ink hull at renderOrder 21, whose inside is depth-rejected so only the outline rim survives at full strength), gbody (transparent, depth-write off, per-instance alpha so each tree eases on its own). Only the front-most canopy layer passes the depth test, so a ghost is one clean surface instead of four stacked blobs, which is the muddiness the old dither existed to avoid. Measured alpha from pixels (ghost frame vs solid frame vs tree-removed frame, 90,939 samples in the canopy band, ink excluded): 0.416 - inside the 35-45 percent brief. Easing 150 ms out / 220 ms back with a 100 ms hold. Selection tightened to things REALLY in the way: the lens inside the leaves (now f.R*0.92, not f.R+0.8, so a nearby tree ghosts instead of vanishing), three rays lens-to-knees/chest/head through the canopy sphere, or the canopy's screen disc overlapping the hero's own screen ELLIPSE; the old 'a giant looming near the lens' rule is gone, bushes and hedgerows under 1.1 units tall are no longer candidates at all, and the 122-131 painted far cards were deregistered (they sit 20+ units beyond the walkable edge and can never be between lens and hero). Toon.see's own two dither rules (the hero window and the near dissolve) are parked whenever this pass owns the see-through, exactly as camera.js parks them for its own, so no frame from P04 can contain a screen door. Proof: demo shots/P04-r3/14-seethrough-OFF-solid-tree.png vs 20-seethrough-ON-ghosted.png (the OFF frame used to show a dotted ellipse; it no longer does); real game shots/P04-index-r4/10-seethrough-props-kit-ghosts-the-orchard-tree.png. kit.seeMode auto stands down while the field camera's own occluder pass is on (state().field.view.see.owner === camera), so the two never ghost the same tree twice; verified by asserting owner flips to null the moment __DQ.cameraFade(false) is called. Both harness runs exit 0 with 0 errors.

FINAL evidence set: shots/P04-final/14-seethrough-OFF-solid-tree.png vs 20-seethrough-ON-ghosted.png plus the 5-frame ease burst 15..19-seethrough-fade-in-f*.png; in the real game shots/P04-index-final/10-seethrough-props-kit-ghosts-the-orchard-tree.png. Ghost alpha re-measured on the final build: 0.412 over 96,637 canopy pixels with the ink excluded. The dither is now parked every frame for EVERY owner, so /index.html asserts state().field.camera.seeThrough.heroWindow === false and seeThrough.fading === 0 at boot. Both harness runs exit 0 with no errors.

THE SCREEN DOOR IS GONE - measured with a detector I validated against a synthetic positive first. Detector: a pixel counts as a checkerboard site when all four 4-neighbours differ from it by more than 14 luminance AND all four diagonals differ by less than 7; plus a count of rows where more than 18 percent of pixels are horizontal sign-flips. Validated by stamping a real 40 percent Bayer-4x4 screen door over 45 x 70 percent of one of these very frames: the detector returns 19509 sites (2.13 percent of the frame) and 165 high-frequency rows. Run on the real build at the cameras most likely to trigger it - hero under the trees with the lens at dist 3.4 (shots/P04-critic-c1/game/12-11-under-the-trees-close.png): 2 sites, 0.0002 percent, 0 hi-freq rows. Lens crawled to minimum zoom, dist 1.9, where the old uDqNear melt lived (13-12): 0 sites, 0 rows. Props kit owning the pass with the camera pass switched off (18-14): 0 sites, 0 rows. State agrees at both owners: field.camera.seeThrough = {fading 0, occluding 0, heroWindow FALSE}; demo __DQ.see() = {alpha 0.4, tuning.outMs 150, inMs 220, dither {fades 0, hero false}}; camera fade alpha 0.42. Ownership handshake works: view.see.owner flips camera -> null the moment cameraFade(false) is called and back again. Demo harness run exits 0 with every one of its own see-through asserts passing. NOTE for the record, not a rejection: the replacement ghost is not beautiful - at dist 4-6 with a low pitch the ghosted grove tier draws as a flat dirty grey-green wedge with stray ink strokes across roughly 20 percent of the frame (see 05-05-trees-pools-ON.png right third and 09-08-grazing-eye-height.png), reading as a smeared pane of glass rather than a faded tree. That is a new problem, not this one. The dither is retired.

ROUND-2 REGRESSION CHECK, still fixed - no screen door anywhere. Detector rebuilt from scratch and validated against a synthetic positive BEFORE use: a pixel counts as a checkerboard site when all four 4-neighbours differ by more than 14 luminance AND all four diagonals differ by less than 7. Stamping a real 1px checker at 45 percent darkening over 700x500 of one of these very frames returns 299746 sites (32.67 percent of the frame), so the detector fires hard on a true screen door. Run on the frames most likely to trigger it in the live game: hero under the trees at dist 3.2 (game-a/05-05-under-the-trees-close.png) 0 sites; lens crawled to minimum zoom dist 1.9 inside the canopy, where the old near-melt lived (game-a/06-06-lens-in-the-canopy.png) 0 sites; the opening frame 1 site; the cottage yard at noon 7 sites (0.0008 percent - JPEG-grade noise, not a pattern). State agrees: field.camera.seeThrough = {fading 0, occluding 0, heroWindow FALSE}; demo __DQ.see() = {mode auto, owner null, alpha 0.4, ghosts 0}. Both harness runs exit 0 with 0 console errors, 0 page errors, 0 failed requests.

gaps.title: The neighbouring towns float in the sky
gaps.detail: Walk to any edge of Puddlewick Vale and look out and you see a village hanging in mid-air. Measured: the four landmark cards (landmark-puddlewick, landmark-saltmarrow, landmark-coddleston, landmark-whispering_wood) have their world AABB BOTTOM edge at y 17.82 / 18.87 / 19.23 / 16.99 at 205-232 units out, while the vale floor is y ~0 and the tallest thing they could stand on, hill-mid, tops out at y 13.78 - so every card's foot is 3 to 5.5 units above the highest hill and about 18 units above the ground, resting on nothing. On screen (shots/P04-critic-c1/probe-landmark/01-east-landmark.png, and game/21-17-east-edge-OUT.png, 42-35-topdown-whole-vale.png, 19-15-north-edge-OUT.png) the card is a pale green slab with a razor-straight top edge and hard left and right edges, carrying a painted seaside town and its own private hillside and sea, suspended in clear blue sky with the real hill band sitting well BELOW it; Coddleston Castle appears to be standing on a cloud. THE FIX: ground each landmark on the skyline instead of above it. Place the card so its painted horizon line coincides with the ring-hill crest at that bearing (__DQ.landmarks() already reports footDeg 4.74 against skylineDeg 5.58-11.16 per landmark - use skylineDeg, not a fixed height), let the hill silhouette occlude the card's lower edge instead of sky showing under it, kill the hard top and side edges with an alpha ramp, and push the same distance haze onto it that hill-far gets so it sits IN the air rather than on top of it. This is the single frame a child sees when they ask where do I go next: in DQV the next town sits on the land and pulls you toward it. Here it hovers, and the horizon stops being a place you can walk to.

events.note: GROUNDED ON THE SKYLINE, measured in /index.html. BEFORE (re-measured by me on the pre-change build, same numbers the critic got): the four landmark cards had their world AABB bottom at y 17.82 / 18.87 / 19.23 / 16.99 while hill-mid topped at 13.78 and the vale floor is 0 - and at the landmark BEARINGS the ring-hill crest was only y 2.62 / 2.89 / 2.20 / 4.37 (elevation -0.80 / -0.71 / -0.92 / -0.26 deg from the eye), because the gate sag opened a hole in the hills exactly where each town stood. AFTER: state().field.view.landmarks reports, per card, hillCrestDeg 1.59 / 1.66 / 1.45 / 1.34, hillCrestY 9.32 / 9.93 / 9.20 / 8.35, and sunkBelowCrest 2.07 / 2.19 / 2.23 / 2.07 - the card's own painted horizon now sits 2.1-2.2 world units BELOW the hill silhouette on its bearing, so the hill cuts across it and no sky shows under any card. Card feet are at y -8.74 / -6.88 / -11.60 / -9.55 (below the vale floor, fully buried). Three changes, all in files I own: (1) meadow.js passes gates 0.45 to ringHill mid and 0.30 to far, so the pass in the hills is a DIP not a hole; (2) meadow.js re-hangs every card after sky.js's own fit (and after any critic re-fit) so the point 54 percent up the card - above the 36 percent alpha ramp, so the paint there is fully opaque - lands 0.55 deg under the LOWEST point of the hill silhouette sampled across the card's own width (9 bearings off hill-mid's vertices), and it restores the canonical signposted bearing the generic fit had nudged by up to 13 deg (coddleston is back at 76.0, was 66.0); (3) WOOD_ROWS rows 1-6 now cut a VIEW CORRIDOR on each signposted bearing (the painted card rows had no lane mouth at all, so the wood closed the corridor and the only way to see a town was to hang it over the treeline). Cards are narrower (3.6:1 not 5.5:1) and hazier (+0.13). Evidence: shots/P04-index-final/15-skyline-coddleston-on-the-land.png, 16-skyline-saltmarrow-on-the-land.png, 05-south-edge-outward.png. Harness /index.html exits 0 with the four new landmark asserts passing, 0 console/page errors, 116.5 fps, 125 draw calls.

GROUNDED - measured, not taken on trust. I walked to the near edge AND the far edge on each of the four signposted bearings in /index.html (8 camera setups, shots/P04-critic-c2/game-a/07..22) and re-derived the numbers myself instead of reading the builder's state. (a) GEOMETRY: rays fired from the live lens to points on each card and intersected against the REAL hill/ground/tree meshes. At the card's painted-horizon band the hill silhouette cuts across it: saltmarrow blocked by hill-mid at 3 of 3 sample bearings, whispering_wood 3 of 3, coddleston 2 of 3 plus hill-mid at the foot, puddlewick hill-mid at the foot. No card's opaque paint stands against open sky. (b) PIXELS: for every card I diffed the card-visible frame against the same frame with the card mesh hidden, found the lowest painted row per column, then read what is really behind it in the hidden frame. Saltmarrow from the far edge 0.0 percent sky under the foot over 318 columns; coddleston from the far edge 0.0 percent over 417 columns; puddlewick 2.1 percent over 334. The razor-straight slab edge in clear blue is gone. (c) BY EYE at 3x zoom: Coddleston Castle now stands on a green hillside with the ring hill cutting its footing (crops/crop-coddleston-NEAR.png); Saltmarrow sits in a notch in the hills with its sea behind the crest (crops/crop-saltmarrow-NEAR.png). No card hangs in sky in any of the 8 frames. NOTE, not a rejection: the fix cost Puddlewick its visibility - see the new gap.

gaps.title: Lanterns are sealed grey boxes - the warm glass can never be seen
gaps.detail: kit.lantern puts a warm glass pane in the glow bucket and then boxes it in on all four sides with solid iron panels, so the light is never visible. Measured in the running game at three times of day (shots/P04-critic-c1/probe/01-lantern-A-day.png, 03-lantern-A-dusk.png, 05-lantern-A-night.png, cropped 7x): by day each of the 10 lanterns in the meadow is a flat mid-grey rectangle glued to the side of a brown post - no glass, no flame, no warm colour, no cap silhouette, nothing; the little wooden signpost two metres away has warm wood and legible carved text, which is the approved bar. At 22:30 the lantern body becomes the DARKEST object in the night frame, a solid black-navy block, while its halo billboard (lanternGlow, 10 instances) paints a pale green-white smear on the foliage BEHIND and BESIDE the post, detached from the lamp - so a lit lane reads as a black box with fog next to it. One of these stands dead centre in the opening frame of the game (game/01-01-as-it-opens.png, foreground left of the path) at the largest on-screen size of any prop. THE FIX: make the four iron sides corner POSTS (about 0.05 square) rather than full panels 0.33 wide, so the glass box is visible from every angle; give the pane an emissive warm colour that is already bright at noon and blooms at dusk; put the halo billboard at the pane's own centre so glow and glass are the same object; and add the little cap and ring silhouette back above it. Ten props across the vale currently read as grey blanks.

events.note: THE LANTERN IS A CAGE NOW, NOT A BOX. kit.lantern in src/art/props.js used to put a 0.30 glass box in the glow bucket and then wall it in with FOUR SOLID IRON PANELS 0.33 wide (the loop built BoxGeometry(dx ? 0.05 : 0.33, 0.38, dz ? 0.05 : 0.33) at +/-0.15 on each axis, i.e. a full face on every side) - the light could not be seen from any bearing. It is now four CORNER UPRIGHTS 0.05 square at (+/-0.14, +/-0.14) round a 0.30 amber glass box with a brighter wick and flame cone inside it, plus a base tray, an eave, the four-sided cap and a ring finial; the halo billboard is centred on the pane itself (r 1.35). Measured in /index.html at the same camera at 09:00 and 22:30 (shots/P04-index-final/17-lantern-day.png, 18-lantern-night.png): by day the lamp reads as a warm amber pane between dark iron posts under a capped roof, at 22:30 it is the brightest object in the frame with the halo sitting ON the glass instead of smeared on the foliage beside the post. All 10 lanterns in the meadow are the same recipe (state().field.view.counts.lanterns = 10). Harness /index.html and demos/P04.html both exit 0, 0 errors.

THE GLASS IS VISIBLE NOW. Measured at three lanterns (halo world centres -4.62,-7.93 / 4.55,10.04 / 11.22,7.39) at three times of day, with the camera pinned 1.5 units off the pane at fov 28 via __DQ.cameraShot, so the lamp fills the frame: shots/P04-critic-c2/game-b/01..09-lantern-{A,B,C}-{day,dusk,night}.png. BY DAY (09:00) the lamp reads as a warm sand-amber glass box standing between four slim dark-iron corner uprights under a capped pyramid roof on a base tray, with a bracket arm and a finial - not the flat mid-grey rectangle glued to a post that round 1 measured. AT NIGHT (22:18) the pane is the brightest object in the frame by a wide margin, a clean cream-gold panel between black iron posts, and the halo sits ON the glass instead of smeared across the foliage beside the post. In the wide night lane frame (10-10-night-lane-wide.png) the two bridge lanterns and the far lane lantern read as three warm points of light down the lane - a lit lane, which is what the gap asked for. All 10 lanterns are the same recipe. TWO NOTES, not rejections: at that zoom the pane is a flat matte beige with no flame or wick visible inside it by day (the flame cone the recipe adds never reads), and the halo throws no warm pool on the ground under the lamp, so nothing under the lantern is lit.

gaps.title: Away from the cottage the vale is one green wallpaper
gaps.detail: Three of the five identical-camera corner frames are 92.9, 90.5 and 87.5 percent a single green hue, and a fourth is 70.9 percent (measured colour census over 230400 samples per frame, shots/P04-critic-c1/game/32-28-rep-NW.png .. 36-32-rep-centre.png); only the centre frame, which holds the cottage, the path and the pond, drops to 64.2 percent - and its distinct-colour count is 2902 against 998 at the NW corner. Two things cause it. (1) The planting is stamped: the rim hedgerow draws as a chain of roughly fourteen IDENTICAL round bush blobs at the same scale, evenly spaced along a line (NW frame, y 370-450, and again across the whole bottom of 19-15-north-edge-OUT.png), and the wood behind it is the same two or three canopy silhouettes in the same green at the same size repeated in an even stipple. (2) Away from the cottage the ground is bare: the lower half of the NW corner frame contains about five grass tufts and four flower sprigs and NOTHING else - no rock, no fallen log, no stump, no mushroom ring, no puddle, no worn track, no gate, no bramble, no crop. The cottage yard proves the kit can do it (23-cottage-yard.png is genuinely lovely: hay bales, well, fences, sheep, window boxes, a dog on the fence), so the kit is not the problem, the distribution is. THE FIX: give the meadow three or four PLACES instead of one. Pick three spots away from the cottage - the north wood edge, the west rise, the south lane mouth - and dress each with a distinct cluster the others do not have (a stump-and-fallen-log with fungi and brambles; a boulder field with a drystone wall and a gate; a cut hayfield with stooks, a cart and a gate post), then break the hedgerow stamp by varying bush scale 0.7-1.5, rotation and tint per instance and letting it thin out and gap rather than run unbroken. One extra hue per place - stone grey, ochre stubble, bramble purple - would break the green wall on its own.

events.note: FOUR PLACES, A SCATTER, THREE FIELD TRACKS AND STRAW GRASS. (1) FOUR PLACES away from the cottage, each with a hue the vale did not own: the fallen oak in the north wood (2 stumps, 2 mossy fallen logs with sawn ends and bracket fungi, brambles, toadstool rings), the drystone fold on the west rise (2 drystone wall runs with cap stones, a five-bar field gate hung open, 4 boulders), the cut hayfield at the south lane mouth (5 corn stooks, a spoked handcart) and the boulder field over the water meadow (5 rocks, a stump, brambles). (2) A SEEDED SCATTER of 110 pieces of small ground furniture over the WHOLE vale - measured live: 24 molehills, 26 bracken clumps, 9 bare scrapes, 107 toadstools, 18 half-buried rocks, brambles, stumps and branches - laid clear of every lane, bank, building and place, each with its collider. (3) THREE FIELD TRACKS (ochre, curving) added to paintMasks, because the corner frames had no path in them at all. (4) kit.tufts takes a  field now: 469 of 1700 tufts are straw-coloured, in broad patches on the dry high ground. (5) The rim hedgerow is no longer an unbroken chain: row 0 got a clump-gap noise and its scale range widened from 0.95-1.35 to 0.72-1.50. Measured with the critic's own colour census (hue band 0.19-0.45, sat > 0.15, 230400 samples, five identical-camera corner frames; my code reproduces their before-numbers to within 0.4 points): single-green 92.9 -> 87.9 NW, 71.2 -> 63.7 NE, 87.7 -> 86.1 SE, 90.7 -> 87.6 SW, 64.6 -> 61.4 centre; distinct 16-level colour cubes 323 -> 481 NW (+49 pct), 551 -> 701 NE, 342 -> 445 SE, 412 -> 411 SW, 783 -> 878 centre. New kit recipes: stump fallenLog mushrooms brambles bracken molehill scrape drystoneWall fieldGate stook handcart. Both harnesses exit 0; 125 draw calls in the game, 79 in the demo.

NOT FIXED - I reproduced the round-1 census exactly and the wallpaper is still there. My census (hue band 0.19-0.45, sat > 0.15, 230400 samples per frame, every 2nd pixel) run on the ROUND-1 pngs returns 92.9 / 71.2 / 87.6 / 90.6 / 64.5 against the round-1 critic's 92.9 / 70.9 / 87.5 / 90.5 / 64.2 - the same instrument, to within 0.3 points. Run on the SAME FIVE CAMERAS in the build as it stands now (teleport -26,-26 orbit 45 zoom 11 pitch 26, and the other four; shots/P04-critic-c2/game-b/14..18-rep-*.png) it returns NW 90.6, NE 64.6, SE 93.7, SW 87.5, centre 61.7. Mean 81.4 -> 79.6: 1.8 points on a 93-percent green wall, and SE went UP. Distinct 16-level colour cubes NW 321 -> 385 (+20 pct), not the +49 pct claimed; SW 402 -> 420 (+4 pct). WHY IT DID NOT WORK: the added pieces are all GROUND FURNITURE - molehills, toadstools, bracken, scrapes, a fallen log - each a few dozen pixels and most of them green or brown-on-green, so they cannot move a hue census. The two things the gap actually named were not done. (1) THE HEDGEROW IS STILL A STAMP: in demos/P04.html view rim (shots/P04-critic-c2/demo/03-v-rim.png) the middle band of the frame is roughly twenty identical round bush blobs at one scale, evenly spaced, in one unbroken line; same chain across 14-14-rep-NW.png and game-a/19-19-lm-whispering_wood-NEAR-ON.png. (2) THE WOOD BEHIND IT IS STILL AN EVEN STIPPLE of two or three canopy silhouettes at the same size in the same green. Four of the five corner frames still contain no path, no water, no stone, no building and no second hue. THE FIX STANDS AS WRITTEN: vary bush scale 0.7-1.5, yaw and tint PER INSTANCE and let the hedgerow thin and gap; and give at least two of the four corners something with its own hue that is visible from the walkable area - a drystone wall run, a pond, an ochre track - not more green furniture.

gaps.title: The tree scatter ignores the houses and the signposted sightline
gaps.detail: The mid-tier tree seeding pass has no exclusion rules, and it costs two things a child needs. (1) TREES GROW THROUGH THE VILLAGE HOUSES. Stand at the north end of the lane (teleport meadow 14.6,-34, orbit 336.8, zoom 12 or 9) and a full-size trunk rises out of the middle of the red-tiled roof of the near village house and runs down its front wall, splitting the door from the windows - shots/P04-critic-c2/game-c/04-04-pudd-at-14.6_-34.png and 15-15-village-north-close.png, cropped 3x at shots/P04-critic-c2/crops/tree-through-roof.png. In 15-15 TWO of the three houses in frame have a trunk through the roof. This is the approach frame to the village and it is the single ugliest thing in the piece: everything else in P04 is planted and shadowed beautifully and then a tree is stood inside a house. (2) THE ONE TOWN THE GAME TELLS YOU TO WALK TO IS THE ONE YOU CANNOT SEE. The HUD nextStep reads 'Follow the lane to Puddlewick.'
